subject: FieldSense 200 Series – Volume Pricing Authorization

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Thanks for making time on short notice. Jamal and I had a call this morning with Ostergaard Process Systems — they're interested in a trial order, but their procurement lead is pushing hard on price. They want to know if we can do better than list for an initial order of forty units.

turns.speaker: Jamal
turns.text: They specifically asked about $775 per unit. I told them I didn't have authorization to go there and that I'd need to come back to them by end of week.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: What's their timeline? Is this a genuine Q1 buy or are they kicking tires?

turns.speaker: Jamal
turns.text: Their ops director told me they have a capital budget they need to commit before March 31st or they lose it. So the urgency is real. They've been using a competitor's unit — Vantecor LX-3 — and they're unhappy with the support response times. That's actually our opening.

turns.speaker: Renata
turns.text: Can you walk me through the margin at $775? What's our current standard cost on the 200 Series?

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: We're at $491 fully loaded at current volumes, so $775 is about 36.9% gross margin. Our target floor is 35%, so technically it clears, but just barely.

turns.speaker: Renata
turns.text: What's list again?

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: $840. Our standard volume break for 25-plus units is $800.

turns.speaker: Renata
turns.text: So they're asking for a discount below the published volume tier. That sets a precedent I'm not entirely comfortable with. If Ostergaard gets $775 for 40 units, what does our next customer say when they find out?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: They won't find out unless we're careless about it. But Renata's concern is valid — we should think about what we're willing to do structurally versus what's a one-off exception.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: My view is that this is a strategic account. Ostergaard has eleven facilities in North America. If we land this trial and they roll out across even four or five sites, we're talking hundreds of units over two years. The margin sacrifice on the first forty is an investment in the relationship.

turns.speaker: Jamal
turns.text: They also mentioned the possibility of a preferred vendor designation if the trial goes well. That would give us visibility into their annual budget cycle.

turns.speaker: Renata
turns.text: I understand the strategic logic. I just want to make sure we're not undercutting ourselves before we have enough market data to know where the floor really is. We're still early.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Here's my instinct. I don't want to go to $775 as a clean discount. What if we structure it differently — $800 per unit, which is our standard volume break, but we include a free calibration service package that has a retail value of roughly $25 per unit? Ostergaard gets the economic equivalent of $775 without us having a $775 line item that becomes a reference price.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: I like that framing. It also gives us a chance to demonstrate the calibration service, which could be an upsell in year two.

turns.speaker: Jamal
turns.text: Would the calibration service actually cost us $25 per unit to deliver on 40 units? I want to make sure we're not just moving the margin problem around.

turns.speaker: Renata
turns.text: At 40 units, the calibration service is probably $8 to $10 per unit in direct labor and consumables. So the net margin is still better than a straight $775 price, yes.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Then I'm comfortable authorizing that approach. Elena, you and Jamal can go back to Ostergaard with $800 plus complimentary calibration on the initial order of 40 units. If they push further, the answer is no — we're already at the bottom of what makes sense for a first order.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: Understood. What's the authorization ceiling if they ask for any other modifications — extended payment terms, for example?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Standard net-30 terms. If they want net-60, Renata and I need to sign off before you commit anything.

turns.speaker: Renata
turns.text: Agreed. And I'd want to see the purchase order before anything ships, regardless of terms. Just to close the loop on my end.

turns.speaker: Jamal
turns.text: Should I also get them a draft spec sheet for the 200 Series, or is that already on the website?

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: I'll handle the materials. You focus on the commercial conversation. Let's plan to reconnect Thursday morning so I know where things stand before end of week.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Good. One more thing — if this closes, I want to make sure Theo's team knows about the calibration service commitment so they can schedule it properly. That shouldn't be a surprise to Customer Support two weeks before delivery.

turns.speaker: Elena
turns.text: I'll loop Theo in as soon as we have a signed PO.

decisions: Ostergaard Process Systems will be offered $800 per unit (standard volume tier) plus complimentary calibration service on an initial order of 40 units, in lieu of a straight $775 price.
Net-30 payment terms are standard; any request for net-60 requires sign-off from Priya and Renata before commitment.
Priya and Renata must review the purchase order before any units ship.

action_items.task: Return to Ostergaard with the $800-plus-calibration offer and confirm their intent by end of week.
Prepare commercial materials for Ostergaard and reconnect with Jamal on Thursday to review status.
Loop Theo into the calibration service commitment as soon as a signed PO is received.
